title: Can a Physiotherapy App Help People With Learning Disabilities to Move More and Reduce Falls?
official: Feasibility of a Digital Physiotherapy Intervention for Adults With Intellectual Disabilities to Prevent Falls and Enhance Physical Activity.
summary: Falls are a major health concern for adults with Intellectual Disabilities (ID), also termed as a Learning Disability (LD), with 30-60% experiencing at least one fall or 6.29 falls per person annually. It's the leading cause of injury and often results in fear of further falls, reduced mobility, lower engagement in physical activity (PA), and incidental loss of muscle mass. Adults with ID also experience higher gait and balance impairments, contributing to greater falls risk compared with the general population at a much younger age. Clinical guidelines recommend exercise as a first-line strategy for falls prevention. While many studies explore the use of technology in empowering physical activity, mainstream fitness research still excludes adults with Intellectual disabilities, limiting the applicability of current evidence of prevention exercises to this population. This research focuses specifically on adults with ID, which remains underdeveloped. This study, led by Physiotherapists, will test a digital tool in the form of the 'Physitrac' app with a tailored exercise program delivered through an easy-to-use patient-facing app (PhysiApp). This study will be recruiting adults with Intellectual disabilities from the NHS Greater Glasgow \& Clyde (GG\&C) health board area of Scotland, UK. This study will have two groups of patient and carer participants who will be randomly allocated using a computer software to follow a 12-week exercise program focused on improving strength, balance and overall physical activity. Strength and balance measurements will be recorded before and after the 12-week program, for patient participants, along with interviews with carer participants and Physiotherapists on their views of using the digital technology. This study will therefore evaluate the feasibility of the app in exercise delivery and explore whether digital data better supports exercise monitoring compared to usual care.

interventions.name: digital falls prevention program through the Physitrac app

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 16 years and over, as per the Learning Disability (LD) Health Register, residing within the NHS GGC Health Board area
* Diagnosis of ID and either: (a) at least one reported fall in the previous 12 months, or (b) identified by health or social care services as fall-risk.
* Able to walk independently, with or without the use of an assistive device.
* Living in any setting, including independent housing, supported living, residential care, or with family.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Any pre-existing medical condition that would make participation in exercise or low-moderate intensity physical activity unsafe, such as a new acute illness or inflammation.
* Participants or carers who do not have access to a compatible mobile or web-enabled device will be excluded from the study, as the intervention requires the use of such technology for programme delivery and engagement.
